Can’t sell it, but generates millions of cash to fund our next experiment, and freedom to do whatever you want is the max it could be.

I wonder if at any point after enough acqui-hires (or worse) people in our ecosystem will step back and ask “WHY” …

Why do we need to grow forever?
Why do we need to tie our future to capital market transactions?
Why do we need to burn tons of money, hoping the next round materializes?

When none of that is in service of true freedom.

Maybe someday the boring path of slowly growing cash flow will be in style…

But I doubt it.

elements.commentary:
Adam Robinson think the biggest point of failure behind signal-based outreach is the implementation itself.

A signal on its own doesn't convey intent. It's a breadcrumb, and only when you combine every signal across every system and time do you start to piece together the full story of that person so that you can make intelligent decisions.

So what I think it takes to make signals work is:
→ Signals need to be scored: not every signal carries the same weight, and the weighting is personal to each business
→ Signals need to be decayed: they lose relevance over time, and at different rates
→ Signals need context from your pipeline: someone viewing a pricing page for a product they don't own is an upsell if they're already a customer, and something completely different if you've never reached out
→ All of that gets calculated in a time window, and you only act once it crosses a threshold
→ There are great out of the box signals (I LOVE RB2B and use it with every client), and also use cases for custom ones like ADA lawsuits filed in Utah (if that's relevant to your ICP)

My point is that doing signals right takes real data engineering rather than a button push and I think that's where software + strong implementation really shines.

results.headline: CEO @ MoltSets & RB2B & Retention.com | Unlimited Contact Data APIs for $27/mo | Person-Level Website Visitor Identity | Helping startup founders bootstrap to $10M ARR
results.comment:
📌 CONCLUSION: I talk all the time about freedom. I truly believe that the pursuit of freedom is why most of us go down this road in the first place. And the path that starts with investor money and ends with acqui-hire is pretty close to the polar opposite of the freedom we all seek.

What’s crazy to me is that most of the people in our ecosystem wouldn’t be happy with an RB2B outcome. Simple product, simple business, stalls at $10m, but requires very little ongoing human effort. Can’t sell it, but generates millions of cash to fund our next experiment, and freedom to do whatever you want is the max it could be.

But somehow the news cycle, peer groups, and investors tap into our ambition, ego, and greed, and make most people think RB2B is silly, cute, or boring.

I wonder if at any point after enough acqui-hires (or worse) people in our ecosystem will step back and ask “WHY” …

Why do we need to grow forever?
Why do we need to tie our future to capital market transactions?
Why do we need to burn tons of money, hoping the next round materializes?

When none of that is in service of true freedom.

Maybe someday the boring path of slowly growing cash flow will be in style…

But I doubt it.

Adam Robinson think the biggest point of failure behind signal-based outreach is the implementation itself.

A signal on its own doesn't convey intent. It's a breadcrumb, and only when you combine every signal across every system and time do you start to piece together the full story of that person so that you can make intelligent decisions.

So what I think it takes to make signals work is:
→ Signals need to be scored: not every signal carries the same weight, and the weighting is personal to each business
→ Signals need to be decayed: they lose relevance over time, and at different rates
→ Signals need context from your pipeline: someone viewing a pricing page for a product they don't own is an upsell if they're already a customer, and something completely different if you've never reached out
→ All of that gets calculated in a time window, and you only act once it crosses a threshold
→ There are great out of the box signals (I LOVE RB2B and use it with every client), and also use cases for custom ones like ADA lawsuits filed in Utah (if that's relevant to your ICP)

My point is that doing signals right takes real data engineering rather than a button push and I think that's where software + strong implementation really shines.
